title: Pose errors became easier to read after two vision models fused their views
summary: On 903 valid difficult image pairs, linear probes distinguished VGGT pose errors with an AUC of 0.935 from its late features and about 0.65 from its per-image encoder. A second reconstruction model showed a similar layer pattern. The signal emerged after the networks began combining information across views.
ai_technology: VGGT; π³; fitted linear activation probes
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; Chalmers University of Technology

evidence.tested: The probes used frozen activation features and category-held-out evaluation, with shuffled-label and image-size controls. The authors also compared predictions with confidence outputs and tested transfer to other datasets.
evidence.unknown: The pairs were deliberately hard and the failure signal varied with dataset and rotation versus translation errors. Layer profiles show decodable information; they do not establish the causal computation or improvements in multi-view reconstruction.
evidence.ai_role: Linear predictors fitted to features at successive layers measured where information about pose failure became available.
